sources.observation: Owned non-fork repositories include nanoGPT, nanochat, llm.c, minGPT, llama2.c, micrograd, nn-zero-to-hero and autoresearch.

nanoGPT is a deliberately small, readable training/finetuning implementation that reproduces GPT-2-scale training, documents DDP/multi-node tradeoffs, baselines, benchmarking and troubleshooting; in Nov 2025 it was explicitly deprecated in favor of nanochat.

llm.c implements GPT pretraining in simple C/CUDA alongside a PyTorch reference, validates numerical agreement, supports multi-GPU/multi-node training and explicitly balances speed, readability, education and dependency complexity.

Neural Networks: Zero to Hero is a course where neural nets, backpropagation, language models, GPT and tokenization are built from first principles in code and notebooks, including manual gradient work and debugging intuition.

autoresearch defines an autonomous LLM-training experiment loop where the AI agent edits train.py and runs fixed-budget experiments while the human edits program.md, the agent instructions/research-org code; the README makes this attribution split explicit.

scope_boundaries: Owned educational/training repositories support substantial LLM/neural-network implementation and explanation contexts, but not sole authorship of every contribution.
Using PyTorch, cuDNN, NCCL, cuBLAS or external tokenizers does not imply implementation of those dependencies.

autoresearch explicitly assigns train.py experimentation to the agent and program.md/instruction design to the human; do not attribute agent-generated model improvements to the human as direct implementation.
Teaching first-principles neural networks is evidence of explanation/understanding and code practice, but course content should not be inflated into every adjacent ML research specialty.
